purpose: Part 8 of the final zero-cost compiler gate: text-only audit of professional_world, legal_practice, and shared_workspace compiled prompts, checking whether they prefer abstract diagrams/blank cards/non-legible notes over fake headings, kanban text, legal document titles, fake case names, business charts, or brand-like software UI, without destroying hobby semantics. No image generated or inspected.

findings.quote: documents (with abstract, non-legible markings only)... No generic laptop-and-coffee office cliche, and no readable whiteboard or business text.
findings.hobby_identity_preserved: yes - 'field-specific tools, equipment... visible physical outputs or results of the work' keeps recognition anchored to the specific profession's material world rather than a generic office.

findings.quote: a device with a blank or non-readable display... No coworkers, no code on any screen, and no readable kanban or workflow text.
findings.hobby_identity_preserved: yes - 'several distinct, personalized desks... different stationery, plants, mugs, notebooks' communicates multiple independent workers through belongings rather than through readable text.

findings.quote: a legal pad with only abstract non-legible markings... No readable case names or large blocks of legible document text.
findings.hobby_identity_preserved: yes - 'case files, tabbed evidence folders, stacked unbranded law books... courtroom or formal office architecture' anchors legal identity without needing readable text; scales-of-justice explicitly constrained to 'a small supporting element, never the sole subject' to avoid the cliche the task warned about.

findings.quote: colored sticky notes, connecting lines or nodes, neutral chart-like shapes with no readable labels... No readable marketing copy, slogans, or brand names.
findings.hobby_identity_preserved: yes - 'blank or abstractly-marked cards... mock layout pieces arranged thoughtfully on a table' keeps the planning-process identity without readable content.

brand_like_software_ui_check: Covered catalog-wide by the shared global_brand_safety_policy section (reused from V1 unchanged), which already forbids Figma-like/Adobe-like/Canva-like/Notion-like/Slack-like marks - not duplicated per-archetype, consistent with the compiler's 'one shared section, not per-risk duplication' design noted in the validation-16 audit's Q10 answers.
conclusion: All 4 reviewed archetypes explicitly suppress the specific text-risk failure modes the task named (fake headings, whiteboard/kanban labels, legal document titles, fake case names, business charts, brand-like software UI) in their own scene_template text, while preserving hobby-specific material identity through non-textual objects. No further changes made this round - the existing grammars from the prior checkpoint (Part B of the compiler-and-review-reduction task) already satisfy this check.
